== Biography ==
'''Robert Glasgow''' was born on '''April 8, 1843''', in '''Adams County, Ohio'''. He was the son of '''William Glasgow''' and '''Ellen (Montgomery) Glasgow''', both natives of Ohio. Robert was the younger of their two children. His father was a farmer, and both parents passed away when Robert was young.

In his early years, Robert left home and moved to '''Illinois''', where he pursued his education at the '''public schools of Monmouth''' until '''1862'''. He then moved to '''Galesburg, Illinois''', where he took a job as a clerk in a shoe store. This experience laid the foundation for his future career in the shoe business.

In '''1871''', Robert relocated to '''Denver, Colorado''', and began working for '''Haywood & Company''', a shoe house, where he remained for five years. His ambition and hard work led him to save his earnings, and in '''1881''', he partnered with '''Thomas Keese''' to form the '''Glasgow & Keese Company''', a successful shoe business. The partnership continued until '''1891''', when it was dissolved, and Robert temporarily retired. 

However, Robert soon returned to business and became the manager of '''The Cross Boot Shop Company''', where he built the company into one of Denver's leading shoe establishments, located on '''Fifteenth Street'''.

On '''April 14, 1874''', Robert married '''Henrietta Smith''' in '''Denver''', and they had four children:
* '''Agnes Foraker''', who resides in Denver and has one child, '''William Foraker'''.
* '''Clyde Glasgow''', born in Denver, who later moved to Wyoming.
* '''Zoe Allaire''', born in Denver, where she still resides.
* '''Robert Glasgow, Jr.''', born in Denver, who now lives in '''Marshfield, Oregon''', with his wife.

Robert was an early pioneer of '''Colorado''' and played a significant role in the growth of '''Denver''', helping it become known as the "Queen City of the Plains." He was a member of the '''Sons of Colorado Territorial Pioneers''', and throughout his life, he contributed to both the public and business sectors of the city. Robert was well-respected, and many of his lifelong friends were those who had known him since childhood.
